campaign-display.purpose: Home promise and reply payoff only, with a 66% desktop optical width that protects its docket gutter.

display.purpose: Public page heroes and policy titles.

title.purpose: Record, capability, contact, and security headings.

body.purpose: Readable forms, policy prose, records, and supporting copy.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase metadata, docket labels, and table headers.

shadows.name: docket-low
shadows.purpose: Separates the active dispatch docket from the navy field.

shadows.name: menu-overlay
shadows.purpose: Used only by the open mobile navigation overlay.

motion.name: button-lift
motion.purpose: Raises public buttons by 2px on hover and returns them on active.

motion.name: route-draw
motion.purpose: Draws the home workflow route from policy check through delivery.

motion.name: route-node-arrival
motion.purpose: Introduces the three route nodes in operational order.

motion.name: reply-link-draw
motion.purpose: Connects the written replied row to its reply margin.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Preserves visible final states without perceptible movement.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The compact cobalt action used for pilot requests and primary public actions.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { min-height: 44px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; padding: .72rem 1.05rem; background: var(--blue, #1550ee); color: #fff; font: 800 .88rem/1 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 160ms ease, transform 240ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: var(--blue-dark, #0d3bc0); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-button-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #ffca43); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Light Button
components.description: The white action used on cobalt campaign sections.
components.css: .ds-button-light-plane { display: inline-block; padding: 24px; background: var(--blue, #1550ee); } .ds-button-light { min-height: 44px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; padding: .72rem 1.05rem; background: #fff; color: var(--navy, #001839); font: 800 .88rem/1 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 160ms ease, transform 240ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-button-light:hover { background: #e8effd; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-button-light:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #ffca43); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Public Field
components.description: The minimally softened field used by pilot and contact forms.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: grid; gap: .45rem; color: var(--ink, #06122e); font: 800 .78rem/1.4 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-field { min-height: 48px; border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong, #afbdd1); border-radius: 3px; padding: .75rem .85rem; background: #fff; color: var(--ink, #06122e); font: 400 1rem/1.55 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-field:hover { border-color: #7e91ac; } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: var(--blue, #1550ee); outline: 3px solid #c6d4ff; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Public Navigation
components.description: The restrained navy navigation plane with one active route and one primary action.
components.css: .ds-nav { min-height: 72px; display: flex; gap: 28px; align-items: center; padding: .75rem 2rem; background: var(--navy, #001839); color: #fff; font: 700 .88rem/1 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-nav strong { margin-right: auto; font-size: 1.32rem; letter-spacing: -.035em; } .ds-nav a { color: #dce7f7; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a[aria-current="page"] { color: #fff; } .ds-nav a[aria-current="page"] { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--focus, #ffca43); text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: .5rem; } .ds-nav button { min-height: 44px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; padding: .72rem 1.05rem; background: var(--blue, #1550ee); color: #fff; font-weight: 800; } .ds-nav :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #ffca43); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Recipient Status Row
components.description: A recipient-level ledger row that keeps written status, time, and attempt count together.
components.css: .ds-status-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr .7fr .35fr; gap: 1rem; align-items: center; padding: .62rem 1.35rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #d9e3f0); background: var(--paper, #fefefe); color: var(--ink, #06122e); font: 400 .77rem/1.55 ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-status-row strong { color: var(--route, #1547d3); font-weight: 800; } .ds-status-row strong::before { content: ''; display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; margin-right: .35rem; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-status-row-replied { box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--vermilion, #bf2e1b); background: #f6f9ff; }

components.name: Offer Metric Lockup
components.description: A compact icon, value, and descriptor lockup used for the four home-page commercial terms; provider approval remains a subordinate asterisk footnote below the ledger.
components.css: .ds-offer-metric { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 3.15rem minmax(0,1fr); grid-template-rows: auto auto; column-gap: .8rem; align-items: center; min-width: 0; color: var(--ink, #06122e); } .ds-offer-metric > span { grid-row: 1 / span 2; display: grid; width: 3.15rem; height: 3.15rem; place-items: center; border: 2px solid var(--route, #1547d3); border-radius: 50%; color: var(--route, #1547d3); font: 500 1.2rem/1 ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-offer-metric strong, .ds-offer-metric small { grid-column: 2; font-family: "Oswald", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif; font-weight: 650; } .ds-offer-metric strong { align-self: end; font-size: 2rem; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -.035em; } .ds-offer-metric small { align-self: start; margin-top: .18rem; font-size: .92rem; line-height: 1.16; }

narrative.overview:
The public marketing world treats managed SMS as an accountable operating record rather than generic SaaS lifestyle theater. Cool-white dockets sit inside a deep navy field; cobalt shows action and routing; one restrained vermilion annotation carries the reply or exception that deserves attention. Condensed Oswald gives campaign-scale urgency while the body sans keeps dense ledgers, policies, forms, and operational copy readable.

The system is precise, near-flat, and editorial. Fine rules, numbered handoffs, recipient-level rows, compact metadata, tabular figures, and mostly square planes make the service feel auditable without drifting into vintage office nostalgia. "Reply in the Margin" is the chosen home-page expression, not a universal page template: the other public routes reuse the visual grammar through split heroes, workflow lines, pricing sheets, policy indexes, forms, and bordered records.
keyCharacteristics: Navy and cool-white ledger planes with cobalt routes and actions.
Restrained vermilion annotation for a reply connection, caveat, or narrow exception.
Condensed Oswald display type paired with a readable body sans.
Fine rules, near-flat depth, square or 4px controls, and circular route nodes.
Operational geometry built from stages, recipient rows, dockets, and accountable handoffs.

rules.name: The Cobalt Route Rule
rules.body: Use cobalt for movement, action, and selected operational state; it is not a decorative wash.

rules.name: The Vermilion Margin Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks one narrow human reply, caveat, or exception at a time; never promote it into a competing primary action color.

rules.name: The Cool-White Plane Rule
rules.body: Separate public records with paper tone and fine rules before adding another container or effect.

rules.name: The Condense-the-Claim Rule
rules.body: Use Oswald to make the claim or number unmistakable; never use it for long policy prose, form help, or dense recipient data.

rules.name: The Metadata Stays Sans Rule
rules.body: Uppercase labels earn hierarchy through weight and tracking, not a second decorative typeface.

rules.name: The Composition-Is-Not-a-Template Rule
rules.body: Carry the palette, typography, rules, spacing, and operational geometry across public pages; keep the three-zone reply composition exclusive to the home first surface.

rules.name: The Record Must Stay Legible Rule
rules.body: Reflow the surrounding layout before shrinking stages, labels, or recipient rows below their usable density.

rules.name: The Flat-Ledger Rule
rules.body: Use tone and rules at rest; add shadow only when a surface is materially active or overlays another plane.

rules.name: The Square-Docket Rule
rules.body: Do not turn public records into a rounded-card system; curvature belongs to controls and meaningful route markers.

rules.name: The State-Must-Explain Rule
rules.body: Pair every color state, route node, and annotation with readable text or metadata that explains what happened.

dos: Do keep cobalt reserved for primary actions, route lines, and selected operational states.
Do use fine 1px cool rules and cool-white tonal planes to separate dense records before adding elevation.
Do keep long public copy in the body sans with readable measure, and preserve all four recipient-table columns on narrow screens through the compact fixed layout.
Do preserve yellow 3px focus outlines and the reduced-motion override on public interactions and route animations.
Do treat "Reply in the Margin" as the home page's signature expression while carrying only its palette, typography, rule, shape, and data-geometry language to other public pages.
donts: Don't apply the three-zone home hero to every marketing route; split heroes, policy indexes, forms, and ledgers already provide the broader public system.
Don't extend this document to authenticated workspace, platform-admin, setup, billing, or provider UI.

Don't introduce beige paper, vintage office forms, typewriter nostalgia, glass surfaces, generic bento cards, or a rounded-card system. The only gradient technique in the built CSS is the monochrome radial repeat that cuts the docket perforations.
Don't use vermilion as a broad fill or second primary action color; it marks the reply connection, a caveat, or a narrow exception.
Don't add testimonials, customer logos, awards, certifications, guarantees, or decorative analytics the product cannot substantiate.
